title: Customer identity lifecycle, refresh and suspension
workflow: Receive evidence-change, document-expiry, official notice or customer-submitted correction
Evaluate effective institution policy and associated product/mandate impact
Transition to review/suspension state with explicit reason and authorized actor
Request new identity proof or supporting source and run dependent risk checks
Approve new verified version only after applicable due diligence passes
Preserve historical identity and restriction decision used for old transactions
requirements: Identity suspension cannot retroactively mutate financial journals or void settled transfers
A new identity document supersedes the evidence claim, not the stable party ID
Changing a legal name requires historical alias and source retention
Closed customer identity must not erase records subject to statutory banking retention
Restriction changes must notify relevant account/payment domains through versioned events
Customer reactivation cannot bypass sanctions, risk, signatory or identity reviewer gates
acceptance_cases: Expired ID triggers state review without deleting party
Unverified correction cannot silently clear suspension
Replay status transition does not duplicate notifications
Closing CIF does not change posted journal balances
Old transaction still resolves historical identity revision
approval_gate: Institution status transitions, retention rules, cross-domain restrictions and independent compliance/operations approval.
